title: A bounded convex set with interior is carried to the unit ball
statement: Let $E$ be a real normed vector space and $S\subseteq E$ a convex bounded subset with nonempty interior. Here convex means $(1-t)x+ty\in S$ for $x,y\in S$ and $0\leq t\leq1$, and bounded means $S$ is contained in some finite-radius norm ball. Write $\operatorname{int}S$, $\overline S$, and $\partial S=\overline S\setminus\operatorname{int}S$ for its interior, closure and frontier in $E$. Every subset has the subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]. There exists a homeomorphism $h:E\to E$ such that $h(\operatorname{int}S)=\{x:\|x\|<1\}$, $h(\overline S)=\{x:\|x\|\leq1\}$, and $h(\partial S)=\{x:\|x\|=1\}$.
